title: Seven countries in ten days is not an itinerary.
subtitle: It is a schedule. Here is what fewer ports actually buys you instead.

text: The urge to see everything is why most people see nothing.
sub: Every additional port is another early start, another transfer and another all-aboard time. Add four of them to a fortnight and you have removed the holiday from it.

items.head: Time ashore that isn't rationed
items.body: Two long days in one place beat four short ones. You get past the harbour and into the town behind it.

items.head: A ship you actually use
items.body: The library, the deck at five, a dinner that runs long. None of it happens on a six-port week.

items.head: Weather margin
items.body: Fewer, longer calls at alongside berths are much harder for a swell to take away from you.

title: Two ways to spend a fortnight
What the seventh port is worth

points.label: Ports one to three
points.value: Wanted, enjoyed, remembered. This is the thing you came for.

points.label: Port four
points.value: Still enjoyed, though the early start is beginning to cost something.

points.label: Port five
points.value: Attended. You go because it is on the list and already paid for.

points.label: Ports six and seven
points.value: A harbour cafe, a postcard, and back aboard to sleep it off.

quote: Any search engine can surface a hundred sailings. The work is knowing which three deserve your attention.

title: Send this to the person you'd travel with.
body: Then tell me the region and the fortnight you have. I'll draft the version with fewer ports and rather more of the places actually in it.
